verdicts.evidence: For n=3, the value a_1=a_2=2/sqrt(3), a_3=-2^{1/3}*2/sqrt(3) satisfies the conditions and gives sum(a_i^2) = 4/3 * (2 + 2^{2/3}) \approx 4.78, which is greater than 4.

verdicts.label: B
verdicts.evidence: The maximum value of sum(a_i^2) is achieved when k/n approaches 8/9, which yields 16/3. For n=9, k=8, the values a_1=...=a_8=2/3 and a_9=-4/3 satisfy the constraints and give sum(a_i^2) = 16/3. The function f(p) = p + p^(2/3)(1-p)^(1/3) has its maximum at p=8/9, so sum(a_i^2) = 4*f(p) <= 4*f(8/9) = 16/3.
